Getting Ukraine’s House in Order

Nina L. Khrushcheva

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has repeatedly opposed the idea of forming a national unity government. But bringing opposition leaders into the cabinet would ensure the checks on corruption and wayward bureaucratic action that Zelensky’s team can no longer provide.

Maksym Kishka/Frontliner via Getty Images

Nov 20, 2026
5 min read

PARIS—Following US voters’ massive rebuke of Donald Trump in the recent US midterm elections, one might be tempted to hope that his malign influence on global affairs will soon fade. Not likely. In the United States, lame-duck presidents often turn their attention to foreign policy, because it is the one field where there are few formal constraints on presidential action. For the seemingly bored and always narcissistic Trump, this means continuing, between the gilded vanity projects he dreams up, to stalk the world like some rogue Gulliver.
